items.title: Dan Wall and Adam Nussbaum interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001
items.q: I finally did get to play with him.

ctx.x: Sure. If you’re in the room, that’s when I said it’s reality. You’re in the room, this is it, this is the whole picture, the complete picture is delivered to you.

Right. I mean and when you feel that amazing feeling from records, the records we all know and love that have helped to shape our whole reality as far as the way we perceive music and play, if you get that vibe from a record, imagine what it must have been like live. I mean so I can’t, it’s really important for young musicians to not just look at the books and look at the videos, but whenever there’s a chance, go out and see the cats play. There’s nothing like it. I mean I remember seeing Dizzy when I was eight…

just made me feel so good. And it was a great thing. And I guess that was one of those experiences that was kind of defining. Although I would never have known it at the time. Years later I said man, and he was like okay. It’s a great thing.
